title: AI_AUDIO growth against a real session

wire_rate_bytes_per_s.label: MEASURED
wire_rate_bytes_per_s.derivation: 2291023 bytes added to AI_AUDIO over 33.41s wall clock, publishing 1500 frames of 1280B each at the 32000Hz/16-bit/mono contract TransportAgent assumes

intended_wire_rate_bytes_per_s.label: MEASURED
intended_wire_rate_bytes_per_s.derivation: 32000Hz * 2B/sample, the contract itself, independent of what JetStream measured

notes: Synthetic silence frames, not real speech -- exercises JetStream's own storage/retention accounting, which is content-agnostic. Framing (20ms frames) matches typical WebRTC frame sizing, not a measured value from the voice-agent Rust source.

This run's duration (30.0s) is shorter than policy_max_age_s (300.0s), so no message aged out during the sample window -- 'after' reflects every frame published, and max_bytes (not max_age) is the binding limit at this write rate; see projected_time_to_max_bytes_s.

P1-2's sizing cited an ESTIMATED ~130 KB/s single-stream growth figure; this measurement puts the actual wire rate at 68571 B/s (~69 KB/s), close to the 64000-B/s 32kHz/16-bit/mono contract itself and roughly half the cited estimate -- P1-2's max_bytes has more headroom than the original sizing assumed, not less. Two frames flowing simultaneously (rare -- one active utterance in flight is the normal case) would approach the original estimate.
